TITLE: Bloom Energy Sinks 9% as Pre-Earnings Rally Reverses; FuelCell Drops 6%, Plug Power Falls 3%
CONTENT: Bloom Energy stock drops 9%, FuelCell Energy falls 6%, and Plug Power slides 3%, with the declines described as tied to each company’s level of AI data center exposure. The article states HYDR is down 4% versus SPY’s 1% drop. It says Bloom Energy’s third-quarter report is the single catalyst for the three stocks and that margin strength versus data center demand is the key test. It also describes the stocks’ afternoon-trading prices and notes that Bloom Energy had closed sharply higher on October 21 after comments from technology leaders about power being a major constraint for AI data centers.

TITLE: Why Micron Stock Dropped on Thursday
CONTENT: Micron Technology (NASDAQ: MU) stock fell 6.3% on Thursday, Oct. 22. The article says rising oil prices and concerns about AI spending dragged on chip stocks. It states the S&P 500 and the Nasdaq Composite were down 1.2% and 2.6%, respectively. It attributes oil-price increases to attacks in Saudi Arabia raising concerns about energy supply disruptions, and says higher oil prices can contribute to inflation and keep interest rates and borrowing costs elevated. It says higher borrowing costs could pressure companies building AI infrastructure, which could affect chip orders for Micron and curb growth expectations. It also mentions that Meta Platforms gave investors more reason to question AI funding, reporting negative free cash flow for the first time since 2012 and outlining plans to raise money through a new class of stock. The article includes a section encouraging readers to consider Stock Advisor and notes that Micron Technology was not among the 10 best stocks identified by the analyst team. It includes additional promotional and policy/terms text.

TITLE: SK Hynix pulls a $150 billion IPO as its own record US listing sits underwater
CONTENT: SK Hynix raised $26.5 billion in the biggest US listing ever by a foreign company in July, and the company has shelved plans to list Solidigm, its flash memory unit, in the US due to market conditions and share price trends. Solidigm had aimed to raise $10 billion to $15 billion at a valuation of up to $150 billion, according to industry estimates cited by the Wall Street Journal. The article notes SK Hynix priced its US shares at $149 in July and that the stock trades below that price. It also states that memory and storage stocks have shed $1.3 trillion in market value from their 2026 records, with SK Hynix accounting for about $489 billion and Micron accounting for about $411 billion, and says 58 of 59 chip stocks in a Yahoo Finance basket are down in October. The article mentions other AI-linked deals being pulled back (including Firmus Grid canceling an IPO, AirTrunk delaying a Singapore listing, and OpenAI seeking a $1.25 trillion valuation in funding talks). It says the next test for memory stocks comes on Thursday when Sandisk reports after the close, and for SK Hynix it suggests watching $149 and notes a move back above that price would put July’s buyers back in the black.

TITLE: Dan Ives Calls AI Sell-Off ‘SaaS Apocalypse 2.0,’ Says Oracle Is ‘In The Toughest Spot’
CONTENT: The article reports that Yorkville Ives partner Dan Ives said the recent sell-off in AI stocks is a “SaaS Apocalypse 2.0,” calling Oracle (ORCL) the “toughest spot.” It states that he described a “tug of war” between accelerating AI demand and the pressure of financing spending through debt and capital raises, and he dismissed worries about neocloud failures slowing the AI build-out. The article also says he sees sell-offs in Meta (META) and SpaceX as buying opportunities and expects next week’s hyperscaler earnings to calm the market. It includes market context that the Nasdaq Composite fell 2.6% and the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index dropped 6.7%, with S&P 500 also lower in morning trade; it lists ETF and sentiment references including SPY, DIA, and QQQ and Stocktwits sentiment. It further notes that in an interview with Bloomberg, Ives compared the sell-off to a “SaaS apocalypse 2.0 on the infrastructure side,” relative to an earlier SaaSpocalypse in February 2026. The piece states Ives commented that the reaction in Meta shares was a “head scratcher” given Meta’s third-quarter results, and it discusses Meta’s share move and Stocktwits retail sentiment. Finally, it quotes Ives saying larger cloud providers can keep spending because customers are waiting for capacity, while the risk is for companies like Oracle funding the build with borrowed money.

TITLE: Zacks Investment Ideas feature highlights: CoreWeave and Nvidia
CONTENT: The article highlights Zacks Equity Research coverage on CoreWeave (CRWV) and Nvidia (NVDA), stating that the feature discusses how stocks could perform in Q4 despite October volatility. It mentions VIX rising to a four-month high due to inflation data, references AI financing debate around CoreWeave’s debt, and notes Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang commenting on CoreWeave’s financial strength. The text also compares market theme performance and broader index moves from the prior week, describing declines in the Nasdaq and S&P 500 while the Dow gained. It includes a discussion of the seasonal calendar window starting October 1.

TITLE: Chip Stocks Tumble, Crushing Investor Hopes for a Long-Term Rebound
CONTENT: Semiconductor stocks were among the market's biggest decliners Thursday. The article says AI-related stocks fell sharply amid spending and Middle East concerns. Lam Research shares fell nearly 9% after an underwhelming outlook that was described as just in line with consensus projections. The iShares Semiconductor ETF declined more than 3%. It also states that investors may have to wait for a sustained rebound after big tech gains. In addition to Lam Research, Teradyne shares fell over 5%, Lumentum dropped 5%, Nvidia shares slipped 2%, and Meta erased early gains to trade 2% lower after sales topped analysts' estimates; Tesla fell 4% despite better-than-expected profits. The iShares Semiconductor ETF (SOXX) was down more than 3%.

TITLE: Tech stocks fall as Nvidia boss warns of AI funding slowdown
CONTENT: Tech-heavy US stocks fell as Nvidia’s chief executive warned of an AI funding crunch and Meta spooked investors with its spending plans. The Nasdaq 100 slid 3% in New York, erasing an estimated $1.2tn of value, while the S&P fell 1.5%. Oil prices also rose, with Brent crude increasing past $112 per barrel. Nvidia’s Jensen Huang said demand for AI infrastructure is high but working capital is scarce. Meta shares fell after the company said it needs to raise “hundreds of billions of dollars” to spend on AI, and it reported large spending commitments under leases and agreements plus a raised capital expenditure lower bound. Tesla shares declined after its proposed AI spending was cut. The article also notes that OpenAI is reportedly closing in on funding at a valuation above $1tn and mentions additional market concerns related to the Middle East conflict.

TITLE: Chip stocks fall as equipment maker Lam Research cites 'supply chain constraints'
CONTENT: Semiconductor stocks fell on Thursday after a major equipment supplier cited supply chain constraints on its earnings call. The PHLX Semiconductor Index (SOXX) dropped more than 6%. Nvidia and Qualcomm fell more than 2% and 42%, respectively, and Marvell and Intel shares were down 9% and 7%. Broadcom shares fell more than 4%, and memory and storage companies Micron Technology and Sandisk were also in red territory. Lam Research fell as much as 11% after CFO Doug Bettinger said quarterly revenue guidance of $8.6 billion would have been higher without near-term supply chain constraints being managed. Applied Materials and ASML declined 7% and 6%. The article also notes recent volatility tied to concerns over AI funding and references broader market context involving oil prices and expectations for Federal Reserve policy.

TITLE: Trading Day: Maximum pAIn
CONTENT:
On Thursday, the article says worries around AI and tech weighed on global markets, with equities and bond yields falling as investors sought US Treasuries. It also notes a rise in Brent crude oil to a five-month high and continued unrest in France. The piece discusses a column about whether the US Treasury will reduce or scrap 20-year bond auctions, citing interest payments and relative illiquidity of the 20-year part of the curve, and suggesting it could help lower long-term yields.

It then lists “Key Reads” and “Key Market Moves,” including reported declines for South Korea, China, Japan, and Nasdaq, declines in tech and the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index, and specific stock moves such as Moderna -18%, Amazon and Nvidia -4.5%, and Blackstone +8%, P&G +5.6%. It also mentions currency and bond movements, along with oil and gold performance.

In “Today's Talking Points,” it says investors’ AI fears expanded beyond spending, revenue, and valuations, and connects concerns about cybersecurity vulnerabilities—described as critical flaws in the PHP programming language and millions of hacking attempts—to the idea that AI-related risks include cybersecurity and potential AI misuse. It quotes a comment attributed to Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella and says the flaws were flagged by AI before serious damage. It also mentions that an iShares cybersecurity and tech ETF rose on Thursday.

TITLE: It’s another horrible day in the markets, and the usual suspects are to blame: AI, oil, and the French
CONTENT: The article says markets fell after a terrible U.S. session, with the S&P 500 down 1.21% and the Nasdaq down 2.9%. It attributes the drop to AI, oil, and France. It mentions CoreWeave falling 10.06% (and down 22% for the year), and Meta falling 6.98% overnight and another 0.33% in overnight trading. It notes Nasdaq and S&P futures were up 0.28% and flat, respectively, before the open. It discusses worries about AI after a report that OpenAI was forced to reduce its valuation sought in a fundraising round. It says oil rose to $114 after a report about the U.S. being prepared to fight Iran for at least another year. It reports France’s 10-year bond yields hitting 5.1% before falling to 5.05%, and U.S. 10-year bond yields falling to 4.9% after a peak above 5.3%. It includes commentary from IG’s chief market analyst about the market moves being context-dependent rather than a bubble popping. It also provides early moves in Europe and Asia (Stoxx 600, FTSE 100, KOSPI, Nikkei 225, Nifty 50, CSI 300), and mentions Brent crude around $114 and bitcoin around $81,683.

TITLE: Blackstone Bet on Chips Drove a Debt Boom That’s Upending Credit
CONTENT: The article describes Blackstone’s investment in AI-related chip-backed private credit and how it helped create a blueprint for chip-backed debt that has grown alongside the AI boom. It discusses Blackstone executives questioning CoreWeave about GPUs and AI, and says Blackstone led a $2.3 billion private credit loan in 2023. It notes concerns about anxiety over AI spending and mentions CoreWeave’s stock and corporate bonds being pressured as investors question whether AI revenues can justify the spending. The piece also describes broader involvement from banks and alternative-asset managers, mentions backstops involving AI chipmakers Broadcom and Nvidia, and outlines examples of proposed or announced financing arrangements tied to chips and customers. It further says the risks of large spending could make debt markets dependent on AI profitability and mentions projections from JPMorgan Chase & Co. about chip spending through 2030, with much likely funded by borrowing. It includes comments from a Fitch Ratings director about how vendor financing at large scale concentrates risk and could create ripple effects if AI disappoints.

TITLE: Meta’s AI spending spree has investors taking a page from the financial-crisis playbook
CONTENT: The article says Meta’s AI spending is prompting investors to focus on protection as they await Meta’s earnings. It discusses how hyperscalers’ spending plans previously set the tone for earnings season, and contrasts that with increased AI-related debt issuance and funding cracks seen in riskier areas of the boom. It cites global AI-related debt totals and references credit-default swap spreads for Meta, Alphabet, and Amazon, describing higher insurance costs compared with prior levels. It also mentions credit-default swaps for other AI-related companies (including Oracle and CoreWeave) and includes a quoted comment about investors using hedging via credit-default swaps. The article explains what credit-default swaps are, notes historical use around the 2008 financial crisis, and states that widening spreads can signal investor concern about an issuer’s ability to service debt, which may serve as an early warning for stock investors.

TITLE: 'A cyclical downturn is inevitable' in an AI crash: Strategist Dario Perkins
CONTENT:
The article discusses a warning from TS Lombard strategist Dario Perkins in a paper titled "Wargaming the AI Crash." It says that while it may be hard to identify the exact trigger for an AI crash, the fallout can be modeled: it estimates US stocks could decline by (at least) 30%, wiping out around $20 trillion in market cap, and it estimates $125–200 billion in losses across debt markets and private credits, with spreads widening and a wave of tech-related defaults. It states that weaker players in the AI ecosystem—described as the neoclouds, Oracle, standalone model developers, and construction/equipment suppliers—would face acute distress, while hyperscalers would suffer serious revenue downgrades. It adds that the traditional banking sector would not be immune. On the broader US economy, Perkins is quoted saying that a cyclical downturn is inevitable, with capital spending plunging, confidence evaporating, and sizeable job losses in the construction sector, but that it would not be particularly severe compared with historical norms and that the Fed has room to cut rates.

The article then says the backdrop for tech stocks has become increasingly fraught in October, citing concerns earlier in the month about CoreWeave (CRWV) and noting that CoreWeave’s corporate bonds across maturities were dumped amid fears of an AI slowdown and implications for its balance sheet, followed by a sharp sell-off in the stock. It also says CoreWeave stock has fallen by 35% in October. It mentions that Meta posted negative free cash flow for the first time since 2012 and said it would issue a new tranche of stock to fuel its AI build-out. It also says Tesla slashed its capital expenditures plan for the year by $5 billion to $20 billion.

TITLE: The AI trade gets a reappraisal
CONTENT:
The article says the AI boom is entering a phase described as “rational exuberance,” with investors pulling back funding and seeking more evidence that investments will pay off. It frames the issue as whether investors can reduce bubble-like expectations without undermining the broader AI-driven economy. It states investors still expect long-term AI to deliver productivity gains, but notes reduced mania.

It cites signs of retreat across different parts of the AI buildout: neocloud companies are described as being hit hardest due to heavy borrowing and reliance on Big Tech backing to build data centers and sell computing power; bond investors are said to demand more compensation for lending to neoclouds, with CoreWeave cited. It mentions Elice’s stock plunging more than 30% in its trading debut and Firmus shelving a planned IPO after investors balked at its valuation. It reports that Nvidia may invest hundreds of millions in Firmus, and notes that chip stocks have slid since the Nasdaq peak on Oct. 6. It also says hyperscalers (Amazon, Meta, and Alphabet) moved from using cash stockpiles to borrowing and that investors are adjusting. The text includes a quote indicating hyperscalers initially financed via free cash flow and are now moving into credit markets, which is described as having an “indigestion period.” It concludes that Wall Street still believes AI will transform markets and the economy.

TITLE: AI Debt Fears Leads Investors To Seek Safer Havens. The 10-Year Treasury Yield Slipped Below 5%
CONTENT: Investors sought shelter in U.S. government bonds as concerns about AI infrastructure debt financing rattled technology stocks, pushing the 10-year Treasury yield below 5% for the first time in a month. The yield was near 4.99% on Friday, up about 3 basis points for the session but still below the threshold breached Thursday. The article describes a reversal from earlier in the month when yields rose to the highest levels in more than two decades. It says investors are weighing risks in the AI trade against persistent inflation pressures and notes CoreWeave as a focal point, with its shares falling 10% Thursday and down 38% for October. It reports CoreWeave’s 9.75% bond maturing in 2031 reaching 15.72% and a five-year credit default swap spread of 1,138 basis points. The article mentions the Fed’s upcoming meeting and market expectations regarding the benchmark rate, and summarizes economic and energy updates including consumer sentiment details, S&P Global’s PMI, WTI and Brent futures levels, and reports about attacks on Saudi oil installations. It also notes other Treasury maturities edging higher on Friday.

TITLE: Chinese Stocks BABA, JD, PDD Slide After Hong Kong Tech Index Falls Below 4,000, Even As US Market Edges Higher
CONTENT: U.S.-listed Chinese internet stocks including Alibaba (BABA), JD.com (JD) and PDD Holdings (PDD) fell on Wednesday after the Hang Seng Tech Index dropped below 4,000 to its lowest level since October 2024. The Hang Seng Index closed 0.9% lower and the Hang Seng Tech Index fell 1.26% to 3,994.77. The article also mentions that U.S. technology stocks advanced as the S&P 500 and Nasdaq rose, with notes about interest in artificial intelligence and developments involving SpaceX and Tesla. It lists examples such as SPCX maintaining gains, Tesla rising ahead of its earnings report, and Nvidia hosting its GTC event in Berlin, alongside gains for AMD, Micron Technology (MU), and Marvell Technology (MRVL), as well as the VanEck Semiconductor ETF (SMH).

TITLE: Meta and chip stocks decline as AI trade comes under pressure: AlphaCheck
CONTENT: Stocks declined on Thursday as semiconductor names fell, with the AI trade unwinding following quarterly results from Meta (META) and Tesla (TSLA). Shares of Tesla recovered early trading losses while Meta sank 6%. The Tech (XLK) sector fell, led by chipmakers like Nvidia (NVDA) and AMD. Memory makers Micron (MU) and SK Hynix (SKHY) also dropped. Shares of Lam Research (LRCX) fell as much as 10% after management pointed to "supply chain constraints" heading into 2027. The piece also mentions Brent crude oil futures (BZ=F) jumping to a five-month high and WTI (CL=F) trading near $100, along with references to other notable stocks being viewed by Yahoo Finance readers.

TITLE: Hedge fund returns worsen this week as tech selloff deepens
CONTENT: The article says global hedge funds were hurt by a renewed tech selloff. It states that major strategies posted their worst day since the COVID-era market rout and that the selloff in big tech was linked to growing skepticism about massive AI buildout spending. It quotes Goldman Sachs’ prime brokerage team noting losses across fundamental equity long-short, systematic, and multi-strategy funds on October 22. The article also mentions Meta and its announcement about issuing a new class of shares, with reported price declines for Meta and Nvidia and a drop in the Nasdaq Composite. It says Asian stocks were also pressured by higher oil prices and fears about hefty AI spending, and that the downturn led to deleveraging among hedge funds. It includes Goldman Sachs estimates for performance during October and year-to-date, and mentions a comment from a TriVista Capital partner about concentration and concerns related to AI-linked trades.

TITLE: Tech Stocks Are Crashing. Don’t Make the Mistake of Selling All of Them
CONTENT: The article discusses a broad decline in technology stocks and cautions individual investors against reacting immediately by selling all holdings that are down. It argues that selloffs can involve different underlying reasons, such as valuation concerns, investor questions about returns on large AI spending, or stocks being sold due to their presence in diversified funds. The piece states that concluding the AI trade is breaking may not be accurate, suggesting AI demand could remain strong while some AI-related stocks still fall because investors eventually focus on the returns from capital spending. It uses Meta as an example, saying the debate is about the return on AI-related spending rather than whether the company can finance it, and it contrasts this with companies that may need ongoing borrowing or equity issuance to fund similar opportunities. The article also reflects on how, during the boom, capital spending was often treated as proof of future growth without enough focus on who will earn returns from that spending.

TITLE: Wall Street loses ground under pressure from rising oil prices
CONTENT: Stocks on Wall Street closed broadly lower on Friday as oil prices climbed to their highest level in more than four years. The S&P 500 fell 0.5% and posted its second-straight weekly loss; the Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 1.2%; and the Nasdaq composite slipped 0.2%. Nearly three out of every four stocks within the S&P 500 fell. Brent crude oil rose 3.1% to settle at $116.72, surging from less than $97 at the start of October and reaching its highest level since June 2022. Several AI-related companies rallied, including Micron Technology, Intel, Microsoft, and Advanced Micro Devices, easing some impact from the broader slide. The article states investors are focused on the economics of AI and concerns about upfront infrastructure costs and the timing/returns on investments. The next round of corporate earnings is described as being closely watched, including Alphabet, Microsoft, and Amazon. Industrial companies had some of the biggest losses, including Caterpillar. The article notes American Express fell 3.7% and JPMorgan Chase, Citigroup, and Capital One Financial also declined. Energy companies rose as oil increased, including Chevron and ConocoPhillips. European markets are described as closing mostly lower, with France’s main index down 0.4%.

TITLE: Nasdaq Futures Slide Premarket As AI Spending Worries Resurface — Oil Tops $112 On Iran Tensions, Supply Concerns
CONTENT: Nasdaq-100 futures fell in premarket trading as concerns about returns on heavy AI investments resurfaced following major technology earnings. The article says Nasdaq-100 futures declined 1.9%, S&P 500 futures slipped 1.1%, and Dow Jones Industrial Average futures fell nearly 0.7%. It also reports crude oil prices surged, with December Brent futures rising to $112.20 a barrel and WTI futures approaching $100, attributed to escalating Middle East tensions and supply concerns. It notes investors are looking at weekly initial jobless claims to be released Thursday morning. It discusses specific stock moves in premarket trading: Lam Research fell more than 7% after its December-quarter outlook roughly matched expectations; Tesla fell nearly 5% after lowering its 2026 capital expenditure forecast; and other semiconductor stocks including Intel, Marvell Technology, and Advanced Micro Devices fell over 4%. It also states Meta Platforms was in the red as it raised the lower end of its 2026 capital expenditure forecast. The article mentions major index-tracking ETFs also slipped and includes quotes attributed to Santiago Mateo of CaixaBank Asset Management about the market demanding stronger returns from AI investments. It further describes Trump’s remarks regarding Iran, and references a New York Times report about plans for possible renewed strikes on Iran, with no decision confirmed.

TITLE: Update: Equities Mostly Lower Intraday as Oil Prices Soar
CONTENT: (Updates with latest market prices and developments.) Wall Street’s benchmark equity indexes were lower intraday as fears of a re-escalation in the Middle East conflict sent US crude oil prices soaring past $100 a barrel again. The Dow Jones Industrial Average was down 1.2% at 52,238.5 after midday Friday, while the S&P 500 fell 0.4% to 7,629.7, and the Nasdaq Composite edged down 0.1% to 25,984. Except energy and technology, all sectors were in the red, led by consumer staples. West Texas Intermediate crude oil was up 3.6% to $103.08 a barrel intraday, and Brent jumped 2.9% to $116.46. Iran’s military is reported as fully prepared for “asymmetric warfare.” The article also mentions reports that the US and Israel have drawn up plans to resume military operations against Iran after November midterm elections, and that Iran-aligned Houthi rebels have continued to strike Saudi Arabia. It states that Treasury yields were higher intraday, with the 10-year rate up to 4.99% and the two-year rate up to 4.67%. It reports that US consumer sentiment dropped to its lowest level in five months and that US private-sector growth eased while employment increased and selling prices rose, based on data referenced from a University of Michigan survey and S&P Global’s flash purchasing managers’ index. In company news, it says American Express reported third-quarter revenue just below Wall Street expectations and that its chief executive disclosed plans to terminate about 5% of its global workforce; it also states that SLB reported better-than-expected third-quarter results and that Deckers Outdoor slumped 5.5%. It additionally notes that spot gold dipped and silver lost.

TITLE: Global markets retreat as tech mood sours, oil prices jump
CONTENT: Global equity markets mostly sank Thursday as tech firms resumed their downward momentum after a mixed set of Wall Street earnings, with sentiment also affected by rising oil prices. The article discusses AI-linked companies’ volatility since June’s record highs, including concerns about large investment sums, timelines for profitability, and higher debt-servicing costs. It contrasts a SpaceX quarterly report on Wednesday that lifted Wall Street indexes with mixed after-hours releases from Meta and Tesla that muddied investor sentiment. It notes comments about risk-off sentiment amid geopolitical tensions and worries about financing AI investment, and that Brent futures rose to $113.17 per barrel amid threats related to the Strait of Hormuz. Tesla is described as cutting its capital spending forecast and reporting lower July–September profits, while Meta is described as lifting its AI spending estimates; their stock moves are given. The Nasdaq Composite is reported as down 2.6%. The article also mentions analysts citing Meta’s spending plans and Lam Research’s cautious outlook related to supply chain constraints, and that investors are seeking low-risk assets. It then says major AI players were yet to report results, and provides a schedule of upcoming reports. It adds that Asian tech stocks sank, including SK hynix and Samsung declines, dragging broader markets.

TITLE: How Are Dow, S&P 500, Nasdaq Futures Trading After META, TSLA Earnings?
CONTENT: The article says U.S. stock futures declined overnight after Meta Platforms Inc. and Tesla Inc. reported results. It reports that as of 10:39 p.m. EDT, Nasdaq-100 futures were down 1%, S&P 500 futures were down 0.49%, and Dow futures were down 0.21%. It also states that on Wednesday the Nasdaq Composite closed up 1.05%, the Dow Jones Industrial Average closed up 0.69%, and the S&P 500 closed up 0.58%. The piece summarizes Meta’s third-quarter revenue and earnings figures, mentions Meta’s board approval of a new class of non-voting Class C common stock to be distributed via a one-time stock dividend (described as a 2-for-1 split), and notes discussion of Meta’s Muse. It summarizes Tesla’s guidance change for full-year capital expenditures, revised timeline for scaling the Optimus robot, and Q3 revenue and earnings figures. It also references elevated oil prices due to U.S.-Iran tensions.

TITLE: Why Tesla's $5 billion capex cut isn't the warning sign AI stock bears think it is
CONTENT: The article discusses Tesla’s announcement that it is cutting its 2026 capital expenditures (capex) guidance by $5 billion to $20 billion, after lifting it by $5 billion to $25 billion three months earlier. It says the change raised worries among tech stock investors that it could signal a slowdown in AI demand, but argues Tesla is not a hyperscaler and that the cut is more tied to challenges of making Optimus humanoid robots than a broader negative AI view. The article includes a quote from Yorkville Ives partner Dan Ives predicting Alphabet, Microsoft, and Amazon would confirm a massive capex spending path rather than cut it. It also describes broader market weakness for Big Tech and references other company and market items, including Meta reporting negative free cash flow amid AI spending, a plan to issue a new tranche of stock, and crude oil rising above $112 a barrel. The article concludes that Tesla’s actions are characterized as delivering the opposite of a capex scare, citing statements about capex, spending versus expectations, free cash flow, and progress on areas such as autonomy and robotics.

TITLE: Stocks Fall Sharply on Risk-Off as Meta Slides -5%
CONTENT: The article describes a broad market decline tied to risk-off selling, with major U.S. indexes and futures down. It notes weakness in tech, including Meta (-5% or more), Tesla, and Lam Research after chip and AI-related stock selling. It also mentions declines in gold and crypto, lower bond yields, oil price strength linked to U.S. State Department evacuations and related geopolitical concerns, expectations for solid quarterly earnings, and market-implied odds for a Fed rate hike. It further states overseas markets are lower, including the Euro Stoxx 50, Shanghai Composite, and Japan’s Nikkei.

TITLE: 5 Things to Know Before the Stock Market Opens on Thursday
CONTENT:
The article says major indexes are coming off a winning Wednesday led by big gains for tech stocks. It states stock futures are pointing sharply lower as the AI trade pulls back. It highlights that tech stocks are declining, with Nasdaq futures down and iShares Semiconductor ETF (SOXX) down, and mentions Lam Research (LRCX) dropping after its outlook. It also notes crypto-related stocks losing ground, including Strategy (MSTR) and Coinbase (COIN), alongside WTI oil and gold futures moves and a drop in the 10-year Treasury yield.

It reports that Tesla (TSLA) shares are sliding premarket despite an earnings beat, summarizing its adjusted earnings, revenue, and comments about sales prices and battery supply constraints. It also notes SpaceX shares are down premarket.

It states Meta (META) shares are lower after initial post-earnings gains, summarizing Meta’s revenue and earnings per share, mentioning legal fees, and its expected fourth-quarter revenue range. The piece also references Anthropic and AI agent competition and that Western Digital (WDC) is set to release results after the closing bell.

TITLE: Morning Bid: Rattled by oil, tech and France
CONTENT: A Reuters market report says the first Big Tech earnings of the season have been mixed and have not shifted main market themes, with overnight index futures weaker. It attributes the risk-off tone across world markets to a surge in world oil prices to the highest level since May and to another jump in French bond yields and risk premia. Brent crude rises to more than $112 per barrel. French 10-year debt yields top 5% and the risk premium versus German debt widens to 165 basis points. Back on Wall Street, stock index futures fall and Treasury yields decline amid risk aversion. It notes Meta shares briefly rose on a slight earnings beat but later reversed and are down 3% as the company burns cash for the first time in over a decade, increases spending plans, and issues more shares. It states Tesla shares slip 5% after an update, despite positive free cash flow, with capex and car sales targets to 2030 coming in below forecast. It says Super Micro eased jitters after a revenue beat lifted its stock more than 10% on Wednesday, but it also fell overnight. A chart section adds that Meta gave up early gains after announcing a new class of stock to fund its AI push, with third-quarter revenue beat and a strong fourth-quarter outlook, and reports negative free cash flow of $2 billion in the third quarter versus almost $11 billion positive a year earlier.

TITLE: Stock Market News for Oct 23, 2026
CONTENT: U.S. stock markets closed predominantly lower on Thursday as AI trade plummeted and concerns persisted about the sustainability of large AI data center spending. Higher crude oil prices dented sentiment. The Dow ended with a marginal gain, while the Nasdaq Composite and the S&P 500 ended sharply lower. The article reports performance details for the major indexes and sector moves, along with changes in the VIX and market trading statistics. It includes a section discussing Meta Platforms (META), noting strong third-quarter 2026 earnings results with revenue growth and higher adjusted EPS, while also stating Meta reported its first quarterly outflow of free cash flow in its history and spent $34.91 billion on AI capex. It also mentions an increase in Meta’s lower-end 2026 AI capex guidance and plans to issue nonvoting shares related to funding AI investments, concluding that META shares fell after the news.

TITLE: Stocks Fall Pre-Bell as Traders Digest Meta, Tesla Earnings
CONTENT: US equity markets were down before the opening bell Thursday as traders digested financial results from Meta Platforms (META) and Tesla (TSLA) and awaited more corporate earnings. In premarket trading, the S&P 500 fell 1.1%, the Dow Jones Industrial Average decreased 0.7%, and the Nasdaq 100 slipped 1.9%. The article says Meta shares were down 1.2% pre-bell after Meta’s third-quarter results, which included a $9.89 billion charge related to a settlement of litigation over teen mental health and social media. It also reports Tesla’s stock fell 4.3% after third-quarter revenue slipped year over year due to weakness in its automotive and energy generation divisions. It mentions other stocks with premarket moves and lists companies scheduled to report earnings before the bell or after markets close. It also covers early Thursday moves in treasury yields, crude oil, spot gold, and bitcoin, and briefly notes reported plans and orders related to US actions involving Iran and Saudi Arabia, plus items on the economic calendar.

TITLE: Stocks fall, but tech shares steady after selloff; oil hits highest in nearly six months
CONTENT: Major stock indexes ended lower on Friday as tech shares mostly steadied. The Nasdaq eased and European shares also ended lower. An index of semiconductors rose 0.4%, and the S&P 500 technology index was also up 0.4%. The S&P 500 energy sector rose 2.5% to a record high, with Brent crude futures settling at $116.72 per barrel and US West Texas Intermediate closing at $103.27 per barrel, both up on the day. US Treasury yields rose after the benchmark 10-year yield posted its biggest one-day drop in nearly four years. Investor focus remained on earnings season, and next week’s quarterly results for Alphabet, Microsoft, and Amazon were noted. Meta shares ended down 1%, while Microsoft was up 0.7%. Shares of Alphabet and Amazon eased. American Express shares fell 3.7% after results and remarks from its CEO. Telecom company shares including Verizon dropped after a report about SpaceX being in talks with cellular infrastructure companies about launching a US wireless carrier program.

TITLE: Earnings flood, Fed meeting will test rickety AI market rally
CONTENT: US stock investors face a pivotal week as corporate earnings reports led by major AI players and a Federal Reserve meeting pose tests for a market rally. Weakness in technology shares has left investors concerned about the AI trade. The Nasdaq Composite posted a slim loss on Friday after its biggest daily drop since June, following disappointing quarterly reports from Meta and Lam Research. Alphabet, Microsoft, and Amazon are set to headline the next round of quarterly results, along with a large portion of S&P 500 companies. The Fed’s interest rate policy meeting on Wednesday could also rattle markets. Investors are also focused on the November 3 midterm elections. The article notes robust US profit growth and that third-quarter S&P 500 earnings are on pace to rise more than 32% year over year, with next week described as the busiest earnings week.

TITLE: Wall Street closes lower to end rocky week
CONTENT: Wall Street closed lower on Friday as technology shares steadied, ending a turbulent week tied to the AI trade. The Nasdaq Composite posted a small loss after its biggest one-day drop since June, with concerns about financing costs for heavy AI investment. The S&P 500 technology sector rose 0.35%, while most S&P 500 sectors fell, including consumer staples, consumer discretionary, and financials. Next week, about one-third of S&P 500 companies are set to report results, including Alphabet, Microsoft, and Amazon. The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 652.82 points (1.23%), the S&P 500 lost 39.75 points (0.52%), and the Nasdaq Composite fell 53.52 points (0.21%). For the week, the S&P 500 fell 0.5% and the Nasdaq dropped 0.7%, while the Dow rose 0.4% for its third straight weekly gain. The communication services sector was pressured by declines in telecommunications stocks after a report about SpaceX seeking thousands of cell sites for a fourth wireless carrier. The energy sector rose 2.5% to a record high, and American Express shares fell 3.7% after raising its profit forecast and announcing plans to eliminate 5% of its workforce. SLB shares rose after beating Wall Street estimates for third-quarter profit, and US consumer sentiment edged down near a record low in October according to the University of Michigan.

TITLE: The AI sell-off is crushing stocks of companies leading the data center build-out
CONTENT: The article says that despite “blowout quarters,” two major suppliers to the AI data center build-out are being sold off by investors. It reports that Bloom Energy (BE) said sales jumped 138% last quarter and raised its full-year outlook to roughly 122% growth; and Comfort Systems (FIX) said its backlog nearly doubled to $17.8 billion. It states that Bloom and Comfort Systems fell again Friday, and that Credo (CRDO) also fell. The piece also cites Yahoo Finance calculations that since the S&P 500’s Oct. 6 record close, the companies building and equipping AI data centers are down a median 23%, including Caterpillar (CAT), GE Vernova (GEV), Vertiv (VRT), and Eaton (ETN). It includes comparisons that power producers are down 14%, Nvidia (NVDA) is off 11%, and Big Tech is down 5%. The article discusses commentary that power is the biggest constraint for the AI build-out, and includes discussion of supply vs. demand for computing power and transformer lead times, noting concern about a possible “scarcity unwinds.” It also states that a dozen of the biggest builders and power names have shed more than $300 billion in market value since Oct. 6.

TITLE: Meta Stock Is Under Pressure as AI Costs and Legal Bills Mount. Here Are 4 Things Investors Need to Watch.
CONTENT: The article says Meta (META) is facing pressure as AI costs and legal bills increase. It describes Meta’s third-quarter results: revenue rose 26% to $64.6 billion and diluted EPS rose 265% to $3.83. It also states free cash flow turned negative, with operating cash flow of $32.79 billion and capital expenditures and finance lease payments of $34.91 billion, resulting in negative free cash flow of $2.12 billion. The piece mentions the stock dropped about 7% after the results and is back in the red for the year. It further notes the company recorded $9.89 billion in legal expense in Q3 related to a settlement arrangement with 52 state attorneys general, with overall deal payments that could reach $18.59 billion. The article states operating income fell 37% to $12.99 billion and diluted EPS fell to $3.83, and that without the legal charge operating income and diluted EPS would have been higher. It also includes statements that negative free cash flow in a single quarter may reflect a planned investment cycle, but investors may want evidence that the investments drive additional revenue and profit.

TITLE: SpaceX CEO Elon Musk is 'one of one': Will the market give Anthropic's Dario Amodei the same leeway?
CONTENT: The article discusses how SpaceX and Tesla CEO Elon Musk is portrayed as uniquely positioned compared with Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei. It says Anthropic is incurring big losses as a public company and raises whether the market will give Amodei similar leeway as it has historically given Musk-led Tesla and SpaceX, or whether it will punish Anthropic and Amodei for not meeting ambitious growth objectives. It includes a quote about Musk receiving leeway due to his persona, notes that Manhattan Venture Partners is an investor in both SpaceX and Anthropic, and describes reports that Anthropic is preparing to file its S-1 prospectus. It states that leaked details indicate first-half 2026 revenue of $16.3 billion versus $1.1 billion a year ago, but also an $80.7 billion first-half net loss. It also mentions reported targets for a listing valuation around $1.5 trillion to $2 trillion and that Anthropic could debut on public markets before the end of November.

TITLE: Dear Amazon Stock Fans, Mark Your Calendar for October 29
CONTENT: The article says Amazon (AMZN) will release its third-quarter earnings on Oct. 29. It discusses why the event could matter for Amazon stock, including expectations about Amazon Web Services (AWS) demand, AI infrastructure workloads, and the advertising business. It notes Amazon shares have gained 8% year-to-date and states AWS recorded 36.7% year-over-year revenue growth in Q2 and provided $4.6 billion in sequential revenue growth. It also mentions Amazon’s guidance for Q3 net sales between $197 billion and $202 billion, and describes a “backlog” figure associated with AWS. The text includes additional commentary on catalysts for Q3, possible limits on near-term earnings growth due to AI investments, and references to improvements in e-commerce fulfillment.

TITLE: How Nvidia Stock Can Make or Break the Anthropic IPO – and the Claude Maker’s Potential $2 Trillion Valuation
CONTENT: The article discusses expectations for Anthropic’s IPO and how Nvidia stock could be affected. It mentions draft paperwork, valuation speculation of $1.5 trillion to $2 trillion, and that Anthropic is preparing to tap public markets. It contrasts Nvidia’s earlier public listing with Anthropic’s current entry into the IPO market. It argues investors should consider whether market speculative enthusiasm remains strong enough for a multitrillion-dollar AI IPO. It also references the Invesco QQQ Trust (QQQ) as an indicator of institutional risk tolerance, describing QQQ’s recent weakness via multi-percent weekly drops and bearish momentum indicators, despite broadly bullish commentary from Wall Street.

TITLE: Apple is taking Wall Street's top spot back from Nvidia — for the fifth time
CONTENT: The article says Apple briefly topped Nvidia in market value on Friday, reclaiming the top spot for the fifth time, though the lead has not been sustained and Nvidia has moved back into the lead. It notes both companies are each worth about $5.1 trillion, with the gap under 1% at Thursday’s close, and connects the flip to Apple’s stock record run and the release day of the “iPhone Duo.” It also provides historical context on prior leadership changes among Apple, Microsoft, Amazon, Alphabet, and Nvidia during the past decade and describes Nvidia’s first No. 1 close dates and subsequent interruptions by Apple. It states the No. 1 spot has changed hands frequently since 2024, and that this time Apple and Nvidia are heading in opposite directions, with Apple up about 4% since Oct. 6 and Nvidia about 11% below its Oct. 6 record close after a chip rout. The article ends with references to upcoming earnings for Microsoft and Alphabet and mentions that internal AI tools were used to analyze and draft the post, with humans reviewing and fact-checking it before publication.

TITLE: A $4 Billion Reason to Take Another Look at Supermicro Stock
CONTENT: The article says Super Micro Computer (SMCI) is in focus after delivering a major boost to its fiscal first-quarter revenue outlook. It reports that Supermicro raised its Q1 fiscal 2027 revenue guidance to $18.5 billion-$19.5 billion from $14.5 billion-$15.5 billion, noting this is about $4 billion higher than the previous guidance at the midpoint. It also says gross margin outlook was raised to 12%-12.5% from 10.4%-10.8%, attributed primarily to a more favorable customer and product mix. The article states the new revenue outlook is above Wall Street’s average estimate of about $15 billion and says Supermicro reports full Q1 results on Nov. 3. It includes background about Supermicro’s business, products, and market context, and discusses SMCI stock performance over the past year and year-to-date.

TITLE: SpaceX Talks Send Cell Tower Stocks Surging
CONTENT: SpaceX has said it aims to make Starlink Mobile a major mobile carrier. Crown Castle shares surged Friday after Bloomberg reported the company is discussing leases with SpaceX. SpaceX is looking to secure thousands of cell sites in the U.S. to support its goal of making Starlink Mobile a major mobile carrier. Wireless carrier shares fell amid worries about growing competition. Cell tower stocks are jumping after a report that SpaceX is in talks with providers to secure thousands of cell sites. Shares of Crown Castle (CCI) were up more than 13% in early trading, and shares of American Tower (AMT) also climbed. The report says SpaceX is looking to secure at least 80,000 cell sites across the U.S. SpaceX and Crown Castle did not respond to Investopedia's requests for comment in time for publication. Shares of AT&T (T), Verizon (VZ), and T-Mobile (TMUS) were each down between 3% to 5% recently. SpaceX shares rose less than 1% after plunging 9% in yesterday's tech sell-off.

TITLE: Norwegian downgraded, Skydance upgraded: Wall Street's top analyst calls
CONTENT: The article summarizes Wall Street research analyst upgrades and downgrades compiled by The Fly. It lists Top 5 Upgrades: JPMorgan upgraded Skydance (SKYD) to Neutral from Underweight with a price target of $9 (from $14) and said coverage resumed after a period of restriction; Phillip Securities upgraded SpaceX (SPCX) to Buy from Sell with a price target of $250 (from $75) citing compute demand and contract pricing; Jefferies upgraded MSC Industrial (MSM) to Buy from Hold with a price target of $135 (from $130), noting a 15% pullback after the earnings report; BofA upgraded Allegion (ALLE) to Buy from Neutral with a price target of $200 (from $164); and BofA upgraded Pharvaris (PHVS) to Buy from Neutral with an unchanged price target of $44. It lists Top 5 Downgrades: JPMorgan downgraded Norwegian Cruise Line (NCLH) to Underweight from Neutral with a price target of $11 (from $13); Piper Sandler downgraded Deckers Outdoor (DECK) to Underweight from Neutral with a price target of $75 (from $100); BofA downgraded NVR (NVR) to Underperform from Buy with a price target of $5,900 (from $6,725); Piper Sandler downgraded Globe Life (GL) to Neutral from Overweight with a price target of $165 (from $200); and Raymond James downgraded First Industrial Realty (FR) to Outperform from Strong Buy with a price target of $71 (from $86).

TITLE: Moderna stock extends losses as investors digest melanoma vaccine trial data
CONTENT: The article says Moderna (MRNA) extended losses on Friday after a sharp sell-off the previous session as investors digested data from a late-stage trial of its personalized melanoma vaccine. It notes the stock closed down more than 1% a day after plunging more than 17% in its worst single-day performance since Aug. 20, and that more than $17 billion in market value vanished on Thursday as late-stage trial details circulated ahead of the official debut. It states that Merck (MRK), Moderna’s partner, confirmed results came out early and that full data is set for release on Saturday at Europe’s biggest cancer conference in Madrid. The article also mentions that the leaked figures did not initially impress Wall Street and cites analyst rating/price target statements from Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley, and Citi, and a summary of buy/hold/sell ratings. It further notes that the company’s valuation has shifted over the summer away from declining COVID-19 vaccine business toward potential in cancer treatment, and references August phase 3 results for its personalized cancer vaccine developed with Merck.

TITLE: Stocks extend declines, 10-year Treasury holds below 5%: AlphaCheck
CONTENT: Good morning. Stocks declined on Friday, extending the prior session's tech-heavy losses. Yields on the 10-year Treasury held near 4.97% after their biggest one-day drop since 2023. Here's a check of the markets in the first few minutes of trading, based on a heat map powered by Yahoo Finance AlphaSpace data. The Tech (XLK) sector fell slightly after shares of chipmakers Nvidia (NVDA) and AMD (AMD) stabilized. Memory makers Micron (MU) and SK Hynix (SKHY) both rebounded. Moderna (MRNA) sank another 6%, extending declines from the prior session following the lead data of the company's melanoma vaccine trial. Brent crude oil futures held near $110 per barrel, while WTI traded near $101 as traders priced in the possibility of escalating fighting in the Middle East. Other notable stocks viewers are American Express (AXP), Western Digital (WDC), and Bloom Energy (PG).

TITLE: Ahead of Verizon Earnings, Here's What Barchart Data Says Comes Next for VZ Stock
CONTENT: The article discusses expectations ahead of Verizon’s earnings report on Oct. 26, including consensus EPS of $1.27 for its third financial quarter and mention that Verizon shares are down more than 10% versus their year-to-date high. It describes options sentiment for VZ, including a put-to-call ratio of 0.60x for contracts expiring Oct. 30 and an upper price level on those options at $46.72, suggesting potential upside. It notes Verizon’s dividend yield of 6.26% and that the stock is trading around a forward P/E ratio of about 8x before the earnings event. It also mentions insider activity, the competitive impact of a spectrum deal involving SpaceX, and a consensus rating of “Moderate Buy” with a mean price target around $51. The page includes a disclaimer that the article was originally published on Barchart.com and information about the author’s lack of positions in mentioned securities.

TITLE: Moody’s holds steady on France’s credit rating as country grapples with turmoil and higher yields
CONTENT: Moody’s decided to maintain its credit rating on France. The agency kept France’s credit rating at Aa3 and maintained its negative outlook. The decision came as France dealt with a week of civil unrest and rising political risk, and investors had been anticipating the rating decision amid a surge in bond yields, with the 10-year bond yield surpassing 5% for the first time since 2002.

TITLE: Nvidia’s Huang heads to Kazakhstan for the first time — and he’s not the only one with big plans
CONTENT: The article discusses Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s first visit to Kazakhstan and his comments that the country could become a major AI computing hub serving Europe. It describes Huang’s remarks in Astana about Kazakhstan’s role and the importance of countries developing their own AI capabilities, including infrastructure to deliver AI services domestically and adapt technology to local languages and cultures. The piece also outlines Kazakhstan’s AI ambitions, including a government plan for a $10 billion AI infrastructure investment with Firebird and mentions Nvidia’s planned investment related to GPU-based infrastructure expansion across Armenia and Kazakhstan. It covers Higgsfield’s presence in Kazakhstan and that Nvidia and TCV invested in an extension of Higgsfield’s Series B round. The article further references Data Center Valley in Ekibastuz and Kazakhstan’s promotion of advantages for data center development. It includes comments attributed to Kazakhstan’s digital development ministry about hyperscale data centers by GK Hyperscale, and mentions that Volkswagen is expanding into Central Asia through its China operations. The article also references SCO-related discussions and AI events in Kazakhstan.

CONTENT: The article says Apple is set to take back the market-cap crown from Nvidia, and that upcoming earnings may push it over the top.

TITLE: AEP and Xcel Energy Face Surging Power Demand. Which Dividend Is Safer?
CONTENT: The article compares American Electric Power (AEP) and Xcel Energy (XEL) as regulated utilities facing new demand from data centers and discusses their dividend outlooks. It states that both utilities yield about 3% and point to earnings growth, but it argues the difference is what could put the dividend at risk. It reports past one-year performance, compares the latest dividend raises and targeted annual increases, and contrasts dividend coverage as a share of earnings versus each company’s target range. It also describes AEP’s contracted load additions and $78 billion capital plan versus Xcel’s smaller data center pipeline and retained 2026 guidance. The piece highlights risk factors it attributes to Xcel, including wildfire-related costs, litigation, debt and a negative credit outlook, and compares these to AEP’s disclosures about regulatory issues and targets for funds-from-operations-to-debt and planned equity. It concludes with a verdict that AEP’s dividend is “built to last,” while Xcel’s slightly higher yield comes with wildfire and credit-related risks.

TITLE: AbbVie’s Dividend Survived Humira’s Patent Cliff. Will Merck and Amgen’s?
CONTENT:
The article discusses how dividend safety may be affected when major drugs lose patent protection (patent cliffs). It compares AbbVie, Merck, Amgen, and Gilead based on newer drugs replacing older ones, dividend coverage, free cash flow, and related risk factors.

AbbVie: The piece says AbbVie yields 2.3% and describes quarterly dividend levels and historical increases, discusses dividend safety using trailing and adjusted EPS and free cash flow, and notes net leverage and negative book equity tied to the Allergan deal. It provides figures for Humira declines and growth for Skyrizi and Rinvoq, including patent-related timing for Skyrizi.

Merck: The piece describes Merck’s dividend level and history of increases, addresses concerns about trailing EPS versus the dividend and suggests the gap reflects one-time charges. It cites KEYTRUDA sales and upcoming loss of exclusivity, and outlines growth drivers and risks related to expected moderation in U.S. KEYTRUDA growth.

Amgen: The article states Amgen yield and dividend increase history, discusses dividend coverage by EPS and free cash flow, and provides sales trends for certain products. It highlights growth drivers and mentions debt as a risk factor.

Gilead Sciences: The piece discusses Gilead’s lower yield, a GAAP net loss attributed to acquired R&D write-offs, and free cash flow used for dividends and buybacks. It contrasts Veklury’s decline with ongoing HIV sales growth and mentions upcoming FDA decisions.

The article concludes with a ranking of the four dividends by “patent-cliff readiness,” stating none of the four show classic warning signs of a dividend cut while summarizing the main concerns and supports for each company.

TITLE: Amazon Survived a 50% Crash. Here’s What a $1,000 Investment Became
CONTENT: The article discusses Amazon’s performance over the past decade, stating it survived a 50% stock drop, a CEO transition, and its first losing year in nearly a decade before recovering. It describes growth in AWS and mentions that AWS revenue rose 36.7% to $42.2 billion in Q2 2026, and that advertising revenue was $19.8 billion in Q2 2026 (up 26%). It notes Amazon expected $220 billion in 2026 capex and that trailing free cash flow was negative at -$7.6 billion. It includes return figures showing a $1,000 investment in AMZN 10 years ago becoming $5,966, with the article providing 1-year, 5-year, and 10-year return tables. The text also covers timing of purchases around AWS/Prime growth, a 2022 decline, and discusses expectations for future earnings and spending/capex. It ends with a promotional section about a report from 24/7 Wall St. and includes contact information.

TITLE: Netflix Is Now Down 29% This Year: Is NFLX Stock Hopeless or Ready for a Rebound?
CONTENT: The article discusses Netflix’s stock performance, noting it is down 29% year to date to $66.29 despite a Q3 earnings beat. It says a cut to advertising-related guidance spooked investors and that the stock is down further compared with benchmarks. It compares Netflix’s performance with Roku, which is up 47% year to date, and briefly contrasts with Walt Disney, which is down 1% in 2026 so far. The article summarizes Netflix’s Q3 results, including GAAP earnings per share and operating margin expansion, and describes management’s Q4 revenue forecast and advertising revenue outlook changes. It also states Netflix’s rebound depends in part on expanding its ad-supported tier into 15 new countries in 2027 and that 2027 guidance will be issued with its fourth-quarter report. It mentions Netflix also bought back $4.8 billion of its stock during the quarter and provides additional commentary on operating income, free cash flow guidance, and guidance pressure related to job cuts.

TITLE: Apple Is Up 28% This Year: Take Profits, or Hold On for the Ride?
CONTENT: Apple’s stock is reported as up 28% this year and at record highs, with the article stating Apple has matched the entire technology sector while Microsoft and Alphabet are behind. It says the company’s newly launched iPhone Duo is driving momentum, with early demand described as solid, though the iPhone Duo is reportedly in short supply. The article also mentions that Apple’s services business adds recurring revenue on top of device sales. It compares Apple’s year-to-date performance to Microsoft and Alphabet, and notes Apple’s weight in ETFs including the Technology Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLK) and the SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (SPY). The article frames a decision for shareholders around taking profits versus holding, and says holiday-quarter results and iPhone Duo demand and availability will be important. It includes references to overlap with index fund exposure through holdings in XLK and SPY.

TITLE: Quest Diagnostics Data Breach Investigation: Edelson Lechtzin LLP Probes Class Action Claims After Unauthorized Access to Patient Records
CONTENT: NEWS PROVIDED BY Edelson Lechtzin LLP. The article says Edelson Lechtzin LLP is investigating data privacy claims arising from an alleged data breach at Quest Diagnostics. It states that Quest identified unauthorized access to its Quanum Lab Services Manager system on October 21, 2026, and that an unauthorized party accessed certain patient records disclosed in a Form 8-K filed on October 22, 2026. The article says Quest notified federal law enforcement, engaged third-party cybersecurity experts, and initiated its incident response, including implementing remedial measures and temporarily pausing access to the system while it investigates. It describes the potentially exposed information as patient records/protected health information, health and medical records in the Quanum platform, and related diagnostic, test-result, and billing data, noting that the full scope is still being investigated. It also describes who may be affected (patients whose personal and health information was maintained in the Quanum system) and says the company has not yet stated how many patients were affected. It includes an overview of legal options, stating the firm evaluates claims at no cost, and lists recommended steps such as watching for notices, placing fraud alerts/credit freezes, and reviewing financial and benefits statements. The article provides contact information for a case evaluation and includes an “About Edelson Lechtzin LLP” section.

TITLE: Amy Johnson Appointed President of GDIT
CONTENT:
Amy Johnson Appointed President of GDIT

General Dynamics announced that Amy Johnson has been appointed as president of GDIT, effective November 3.

The release states Johnson is a 27-year veteran of General Dynamics Mission Systems and has held increasingly senior roles in engineering, engineering management and business leadership across cybersecurity, defense electronics, space and intelligence systems, most recently as vice president and general manager for Space, Cyber and Intelligence. It also states she earned bachelor’s and master’s degrees in computer science and computer systems engineering.

The release includes a quote from Phebe Novakovic, CEO of General Dynamics.

It describes GDIT as delivering digital modernization, cloud computing, artificial intelligence, cybersecurity and software development solutions to the U.S. federal government, defense, intelligence agencies and other customers. It also states GDIT is a business unit of General Dynamics and provides details about General Dynamics’ businesses and employment and revenue in 2025.

It lists “SOURCE General Dynamics.”
